The year is 3012, and mankind was finally reminded that it was but a speck in the cosmic scale. A solar flare of a scale never experienced, both to this comparatively infant civilization as well as the age-old universe, ravaged through space, in an instant rendering humanity’s achievement of complete mastery over Earth moot. Once a Type 1 civilization able to bend the planet to its whims and fancies, humans were once again reminded over its early, fragile roots, where anthropocentrism was merely a dream, and a non-benevolent nature was the reality.

With their advanced technology gone, the earliest and most personal reminder of the new normal in this world was the vastly reduced lifespan. Most humans were dead before they were even considered an adolescent before the flare. Meanwhile, the harsh climate unleashed by the destruction of their weather-controlling satellites – mankind’s feeble attempt to play god, dispersed humanity all across the planet.

Yet, despite the losses due to this previously unfathomable cosmic force, mankind still retained a key trait – its vanity. The solar flare might have reminded mankind of its impermanence and speck-like scale in the greater universe, but it also steeled their resolve to leave behind a legacy. Something that will stand the test of time long after humans with their now-shortened lifespans disappear, a final defiant stand against all the universe can throw at them. And their answer was the Museum of Memories.

There is nothing more worthy to carry on the legacy of humans than a shared, collective consciousness of their perception of the world. Knowledge, artefacts, and even personal memories individually all fall short of being the legacy of humanity, its gravestone marker long after the last man draws his last breath. Only the collective, the thoughts of all humans shaped into a singular worldview, is worthy of this heavy title.

The Museum of Memories thus becomes a place for people to contribute to this common collective, bringing fragments of their life and memories to be woven together into something greater. A representation of humanity meant to last long after the last of their kind draws its last breath, self-curated by all whom it was meant to represent. And the museum is not merely a shell – a storage for what’s within, but instead also reflects this legacy.

With their now shortened lifespans, time flows faster for humanity. So much more of their individual lifespan happens within so much less time. A second is still a second, but now each one is much more precious. And in an attempt to craft out this legacy before their time is up, the museum is curated, and re-curated, over and over again, its ever changing form much like the dynamic landscapes of the delta it is situated in.

Yet, with this ever-evolving refinement backdroped by a ticking clock, humanity’s route to perfecting their legacy is not without obstacles. As the aggregate of the individual, each iteration of the collective is invariably different from each other, at times almost indiscernible yet at other times distinctly different. Every journey to the museum is marked by an uncanniness,

Thus the question remain: will humanity be able to craft out its legacy and immortalize it in The Museum of Memories? Or will the tension between the individual and the collective, the visitor and the architecture, prove too much a challenge as humanity’s last mission?
